responses.rationale: The core bug is real: get_backup() constructs BackupRecord without reading .pz-auto, so direct callers get incorrect auto metadata. The stated GUI-card impact is overstated because the index cards use list_backups(), which already reads the marker, but the returned record is still wrong.

The singleton initialization is an unlocked check-then-set. Under Flask's threaded request handling, two WatcherManager instances can be created and route state can split across them. The exact 'first vs second' wording is order-dependent, but the race is legitimate.

Holding SaveWatcher._lock across create_backup() is poor concurrency and can delay pause/cancel/on_modified handling, but the inotify-overflow argument is overstated. In watchdog, emitter threads generally drain kernel events into an internal queue while the dispatcher invokes handlers, so a blocked handler does not directly imply the kernel queue fills. This is a performance/contention issue, not clearly a silent event-loss major bug as written.

The None case is real: row[2]/row[3]/row[4] being NULL is converted to 0, making unknown coordinates appear known. The x=0.0 part has no output difference, but the NULL-to-zero behavior is a legitimate bug.

It is true that sqlite3.Connection's context manager does not close the connection. However, in these functions the connection is a local variable that becomes unreachable when the function returns, so on CPython this does not accumulate leaked handles across a long GUI session. A contextlib.closing() change would be cleaner and more portable, but the described accumulating file-handle leak is overstated.
The CLI config command casts user input with float()/int() outside ClickException handling. Bad input will escape as a raw ValueError rather than a clean Click error.
api_watcher_save() calls manager.watch(save) without passing the configured cooldown, so per-save watching uses SaveWatcher's default 300 seconds instead of backup_cooldown_minutes.
The template renders only all_backups[:50]. The heading includes the total count, but there is no explicit 'showing 50 of N' notice or way to access older entries, so the UX issue is valid.
import flask inside gui_command() is unused. Removing it is safe cleanup.
_SANE_NAME_RE already rejects names longer than 200 characters before the len(value.strip()) > 200 check, so the later check is unreachable for overlong input.

rename_backups_for_save() relies on Path.rename() to fail when the destination backup directory exists. preflight_rename() has a clearer explicit collision check, so adding the same check directly would improve diagnostics and direct-call safety.

new_findings.title: Renaming a watched save also drops configured watcher cooldown
new_findings.description: api_rename_save() recreates the watcher with manager.watch(new_save) and does not pass backup_cooldown_seconds. A save watched through the global watcher with a configured cooldown reverts to the hardcoded 300-second default after rename.

new_findings.title: WatcherManager mutates watcher state without synchronization
new_findings.description: Even if get_manager() is made thread-safe, WatcherManager.watch(), unwatch(), start(), and stop() mutate _watchers, _watches, _observer, and _running without a manager-level lock. Concurrent Flask requests can double-schedule a save, unschedule while starting, or observe inconsistent running/watch state.
